ast/async.description: A function called with async and its future awaited, 5M times: S++ only, as C has no equivalent and Rust's needs an executor

ast/binary_expression.description: Each integer operator family in a hot loop: checked + - * / %, comparisons, bitwise and shifts

ast/calls.description: Calls by position and by keyword, an override on a sup extension called directly, and function values called indirectly through a function kept out of line (each indirect call carries the CFI check)

ast/case_expression.description: A dense eight-way case on LCG values in a hot loop: a jump table or a compare chain

ast/case_patterns.description: Case on tuples, arrays and objects with destructuring patterns, guards and else branches, and the is expression, on LCG values in a hot loop

ast/closure_expression.description: A closure capturing a value, called in a hot loop: should inline to the bare arithmetic

ast/defer.description: A defer in a scope entered 100M times; the C and Rust equivalents run the same statement at the scope's end, so the gap is what defer costs

ast/error_flow.description: Results built and propagated with ? through two calls, matched, about one in 97 failing; the not keyword and early ret

ast/gen_delegation.description: A generator that delegates to another with gen with, iterated, and the same driven by hand with res; the C and Rust equivalents are plain loops, so the gap is the coroutines' overhead
gaps: coroutine frames that are not elided

ast/gen_expression.description: Sum over a generator of 50M values; the C and Rust equivalents are a plain loop and a range iterator, so the gap is the generator's overhead
gaps: coroutine frames that are not elided

ast/literals.description: Every literal kind built in a hot loop (integers, floats, booleans, chars, strings, tuples, explicit and repeated arrays) and indexed: all of it should fold into registers

ast/locals.description: Lets (initialised and not), assignment, tuple, array and object destructuring, inner scopes and scope expressions in a hot loop: none of it should cost anything once SROA has run

ast/loops.description: Iterable loops over ranges with skip, exit carrying a value and a loop-else, nested: about 125M inner iterations

ast/members.description: A class with a static constructor and methods taking &self and &mut self, its fields read and written, and a write through a &mut parameter's deref, in a hot loop

ast/object_initializer.description: A small Copy class built, passed by value and read field by field in a hot loop: should stay in registers

ast/postfix_expression_operator_function.description: Recursive Fibonacci of 39: about 200M calls and returns that cannot be inlined away

ast/slices.description: A sliding window over a Vec: a slice taken per step (about 100M of them) and summed by index

codegen/checked_add_in_place.description: k added in place to every element of a 4096-element Vec[S64], 50K times: a checked add per element, indexed up to the Vec's own length; C traps signed overflow and Rust has overflow checks, so all three check

codegen/checked_dot.description: Dot product of two 4096-element Vec[S64], 50K times: a checked multiply and add per element into one sum; C traps signed overflow and Rust has overflow checks, so all three check

codegen/checked_map.description: c[i] = a[i] * 3 + b[i] over 4096-element Vec[S64], 50K times: a checked multiply and add per element, written back, no reduction; C traps signed overflow and Rust has overflow checks, so all three check

codegen/checked_sum.description: A 4096-element Vec[S64] summed by index 50K times: a checked add into one running total per element; C traps signed overflow and Rust has overflow checks, so all three check

codegen/drops.description: A small Vec allocated, filled, read and dropped 50M times: allocation, drop emission, temporaries

codegen/iter_adapters.description: iter_ref then map, filter and fold over a 4096-element Vec[U64], 50K times (205M elements, in L1); C is the hand-fused loop and Rust the same adapter chain, so the gap is the coroutine adapters'

codegen/iter_mut.description: A 4096-element Vec[U64] rewritten in place through iter_mut 50K times (205M elements, in L1); the C and Rust equivalents are a pointer loop and slice::iter_mut, so the gap is the coroutine iterator's

codegen/iter_ref.description: A 4096-element Vec[U64] summed through iter_ref 50K times (205M elements, in L1); the C and Rust equivalents are a pointer loop and slice::iter, so the gap is the coroutine iterator's

codegen/variants.description: Optional values built (one in five empty), widened from Some to Opt and matched, 100M times

programs/bytecode-vm.description: A register bytecode interpreter running 30M iterations: dense case dispatch (a jump table), Vec reads, U64 arithmetic

programs/collatz.description: Longest Collatz chain below 1M: U64 arithmetic, nested conditional loops, case

programs/fannkuch.description: Fannkuch-redux for n=10: small fixed arrays, permutations, swaps, nested exits

programs/fnv1a.description: FNV-1a over 200M bytes from an LCG: wrapping multiply, xor, shifts

programs/mandelbrot.description: Mandelbrot set membership on a 1800x1800 grid, 50 iterations: F64 arithmetic, early exit

programs/matmul.description: Integer matrix multiply, 700x700 S64 in Vecs: checked multiply-add, strided reads
gaps: no SIMD in the std, and the CPU is baseline x86-64 for all three

programs/nbody.description: N-body simulation of 5 bodies for 5M steps: F64 in fixed arrays, sqrt, nested loops

programs/popcount.description: SWAR population count (Hacker's Delight 5-2) of 100M LCG values: masks, shifts, wrapping arithmetic
gaps: no popcount peephole: LLVM may or may not recognise the SWAR form for any of the three

programs/sieve.description: Sieve of Eratosthenes to 20M: a Vec[Bool], nested counted loops, indexed reads and writes

programs/spectral-norm.description: Spectral norm of a 2000x2000 matrix, 10 rounds: F64, sqrt, calls taking Vec borrows

programs/startup.description: An empty program: process start-up, the runtime's initialisation and exit. Its time is mostly the loader's; its instruction count is the part that is the language's
